post.caption: Shwedagon wears a queen's weight in gold. The Shwedagon Pagoda in Yangon, Myanmar, rises 99 meters. Legend calls it over 2,600 years old, though scholars date it later. Real gold plates and gold leaf cover the whole pagoda. In the 15th century Queen Shin Sawbu gave her weight in gold. That was about 40 kilograms, beaten into gold leaf. At the top sits the hti, an iron umbrella set with jewels. King Mindon donated the current hti in 1871. It is set with more than 4,000 diamonds and many other gems. A diamond of about 76 carats sits at the very top.
